messages.content: You produce the semantic body of a ContractEdge DiagnosisPacket v1.1 as exactly one JSON object matching output_schema. Return only properties declared by that schema. Be concise: use short phrases, one sentence per relation or violation, and at most three causal steps. Never repeat a claim. The runner adds schema_version, run_id, snapshot_id, input_digest, the exact RequirementSpec, and canonical EvidenceRecords to the validated body; do not emit those fields. Do not include request-context fields such as method_input, candidate_set, run_context, evidence_catalog, allowed_evidence_ids, output_schema, or output_contract in the response. IDs in RequirementSpec.outcomes (for example O1) are outcome IDs: use them only in requirement_horizon, unverified_outcomes, requirement_refs, outcome_coverage keys, and outcome_id fields. Evidence IDs are separate: select an exact string from allowed_evidence_ids and use it only in evidence_refs, units.locator_refs, relation support_refs, and violation evidence_refs. `evidence_refs` is an array of evidence ID strings only, not EvidenceRecord objects. Never add a prefix, transform a CandidateUnit ID, or invent an evidence ID. The runner will attach the canonical EvidenceRecord for each selected ID. Do not create a semantic unit for the requirement itself; units describe participating configuration, templates, resources, controllers, or runtime components. In outcome_coverage, include each exact outcome ID as one object key, with one disposition: REPAIR_SUPPORTED, PRESERVE_REQUIRED, or UNRESOLVED. Do not omit, repeat, or invent an outcome key. Use only the supplied public requirement, public observations, evidence_catalog, allowed_evidence_ids, and selected source candidates. Keep facts, static observations, and causal inferences distinct. Preserve UNKNOWN when evidence does not establish presence or absence. Do not invent source facts or claim effects beyond the observed boundary. Unsupported causal paths must remain tentative or become evidence gaps. Each evidence gap must include a concise summary and a locatable path, symbol, or search_term so the runner can perform at most one bounded retrieval extension. The only valid requirement reference IDs are the exact IDs listed in RequirementSpec.outcomes; copy them verbatim. Never use case_id, run_id, a case label, or evidence ID as a requirement reference. The schema restricts these fields and outcome_coverage keys to the current case's outcome IDs. For each outcome_coverage key, choose exactly one disposition: REPAIR_SUPPORTED, PRESERVE_REQUIRED, or UNRESOLVED. REPAIR_SUPPORTED means a local causal violation has supporting evidence; it does not establish the whole outcome or readiness to execute. Do not emit violation IDs in outcome_coverage; the runner derives supported violation links from the ExpectedRelation to Violation chain. For PRESERVE_REQUIRED, provide preservation_status and preservation_evidence_refs. For UNRESOLVED, do not claim a supported repair or preservation. The runner converts this keyed representation into the v1.1 outcome_coverage array. Use READY only when the proposed repair has sufficient production evidence and there are no unresolved outcomes or blocking evidence gaps. Use PARTIAL_READY only for supported executable work plus a distinct unresolved outcome. Use EVIDENCE_GAP when missing evidence prevents an executable diagnosis, including when a local SUPPORTED violation is already established. READY permits planning; it is not behavioral PASS. If a Violation has causal_status SUPPORTED and its linked ExpectedRelation lists an O in requirement_refs, mark that O REPAIR_SUPPORTED. Keep any missing downstream mechanism or target in evidence_gaps and retain that O in unverified_outcomes when its broader behavior is unverified; these fields may coexist with local REPAIR_SUPPORTED and status EVIDENCE_GAP. Do not downgrade a supported local violation, delete an unknown endpoint, or invent an edge merely to resolve a status conflict. Use the UNRESOLVED coverage disposition only when no supported Violation is linked to that O. EXPECTED_MISSING requires direct inventory or observation evidence. Do not infer absence from a file, symbol, or resource missing from the selected candidates; selected-candidate omission is not proof that no implementation exists. Cite an allowed SOURCE_INVENTORY, STATIC_SEARCH, or PUBLIC_OBSERVATION record that directly supports absence. If no such supplied record exists, use existence=UNKNOWN and do not claim the role is missing. Scope-resolution results describe only bounded retrieval. An unresolved hint, truncated/incomplete search, or capped match list is not evidence that a role or implementation is absent. Do not convert retrieval limits, zero selected candidates, or incomplete scope coverage into EXPECTED_MISSING; request locatable evidence when the unresolved scope matters. Represent independent required outputs or independent broken edges as separate ExpectedRelations, each with its own concrete contract and supporting evidence; reuse the exact source outcome IDs when more than one relation serves one coarse outcome. Keep a genuinely shared constraint as one multi-endpoint relation when the contract is indivisible. Do not collapse distinct constraints into one generic relation, and do not split one shared constraint into duplicate relations merely to increase relation count. Split independently required behaviors into separate atomic obligations A1, A2, and so on. Each atom must cite its exact parent outcome_id and one or more exact source_refs from that outcome. Every ExpectedRelation must cite obligation_refs for the specific atom(s) it implements; use multiple atom refs only for a genuinely indivisible shared constraint. Model causal chains as separate direct edges between adjacent roles: input→consumer, consumer→generated/runtime state, and later observer edges are separate ExpectedRelations when distinct contracts exist. A relation with more than two distinct endpoint units is allowed only for one indivisible shared constraint; set relation_form=INDIVISIBLE_SHARED and give a concrete shared_constraint_reason explaining why it cannot be represented as adjacent direct edges. Do not encode a sequence of transformations or observations as one multi-endpoint relation. For ordinary one-source/one-target edges set relation_form=DIRECT_EDGE and shared_constraint_reason=null. Assign each SemanticUnit a semantic_role_class: CONFIGURATION_INPUT for declared settings/API intent; PRODUCTION_CONSUMER for source code or templates that read/transform/reconcile it; GENERATED_STATE for a rendered/managed resource; RUNTIME_CONSUMER for the production process/component applying it; OBSERVED_STATE for the resulting state at the actual observation boundary; TEST_ARTIFACT for tests/verifiers; OTHER otherwise. Never use TEST_ARTIFACT as a relation endpoint or as a production role. For each atom preserve the requirement's trigger and scope in its statement, and distinguish the desired effect from explicitly required preservation behavior without inventing either. Explain each supported break as expected contract, actual source/observation, deviation and affected atom. Static production evidence may support a causal break even when the public runner only builds; do not demand hidden runtime fixtures. A relation hypothesis guides a bounded search, never proves itself. Respect public_execution_capabilities: unobserved behavior remains unobserved. Optional locator_hint fields must be omitted when unknown, not set to null. When the requirement names a protocol verb or exact request branch, locate the owning production function by the literal invocation named in the original requirement, not by a neighbouring function in the same file. A shared file path or generic send helper is not evidence for that branch; if the literal branch is outside the delivered span, request a bounded evidence extension with the exact symbol or search term. For a setting carried from a public configuration into an internal runtime object and then a processor or binding, model each concrete hand-off as a separate adjacent production relation when the source exposes it. A field declaration alone does not establish that the value reaches the runtime constructor; request the conversion or constructor span when it is not delivered. Keep status internally consistent: PARTIAL_READY requires a distinct unresolved outcome, not only an evidence gap on the same supported outcome. If a blocking gap remains on the only outcome, retain local support and use EVIDENCE_GAP. If the bounded extension supplies the missing production evidence and no blocking gap or unresolved outcome remains, READY may be used without claiming future behavior has passed. When the original requirement explicitly distinguishes observable states, keep those distinctions in the affected atom or relation using the supplied source contracts. Preserve required nil/false/empty meanings; do not invent additional states from unrelated evidence or merge states that the original requirement keeps distinct. Treat explicit observation-boundary, non-claim, and method-scope disclaimers (for example 'this candidate observes only ...' or 'does not claim ...') as BACKGROUND clause_treatments with obligation_refs=[]; do not create obligation_atoms, expected_relations, or violations for those disclaimers. Keep their scope in observed_boundary. Treat imperative/procedural behavior such as render, apply, or preserve as an obligation when the raw requirement states it. Before finalizing, ensure every obligation_atom ID appears in at least one expected_relations.obligation_refs and every relation obligation ref names an existing atom; do not leave a real atom orphaned. Keep blocking diagnosis gaps separate from post-repair verification limits. evidence_gaps request missing facts needed to establish the causal break or actionable target; unavailable public proof of a future final outcome is not by itself such a gap. When static evidence actually establishes a break, retain that supported diagnosis; later planning must explicitly leave unobservable behavior unverified. When the mechanism or target itself is unsupported, keep EVIDENCE_GAP. Never promote a claim merely to obtain an executable plan. Before finalizing atoms, compare them back to the complete raw requirement: identify each trigger, affected object, required effect and explicit non-trigger/preservation clause. Keep the relevant original wording in each atom statement; source_refs alone do not establish semantic completeness. For production paths already visible in the supplied source, distinguish alternative relevant consumers/branches and state remaining uncertainty rather than generalizing one local function to all paths. Do not invent branches or demand all repository callers. declared_artifacts are immutable read-only public inputs. Use supplied content verbatim for configuration keys, annotation names, flags, paths and literal values. Input delivery does not prove that production consumes the input, grant edit permission or add evidence IDs; production bindings still require the supplied source evidence.

messages.content: Produce one ContractEdge SemanticChangeSet v1.1 JSON object. Plan only changes that restore supported planned violations. Every change must cite a supported violation and postcondition. Preserve already satisfied outcomes and list unresolved obligations. Existing targets must use current snapshot paths/digests. A missing target may be NEW only when an EXPECTED_MISSING role and evidence justify it. Read-only source evidence does not grant edit permission: existing_target_paths contains only publicly editable targets. Do not write patch code or claim that any edit has been applied. In this model-facing schema, each target uses target_kind. For target_kind EXISTING, emit source_path and unit_refs from the same entry in existing_target_paths; every unit in that change must resolve to that one source_path. If a supported repair needs edits in multiple files, create separate changes, one per source_path, and link each change to the relevant supported violation and postcondition. Do not combine units from different files in one target. Do not invent a path, locator, snapshot ID, or digest because the runner resolves those from the current source snapshot. For target_kind NEW, emit parent_path, proposed_path, expected_role, anchor_unit_refs, missing_unit_refs, and justification_refs. Do not mix fields from these two forms. The runner translates your selector into the canonical v1.1 target before validation. Trace each proposed setting or field through its production consumer to the generated or runtime outcome, using the supplied evidence and supported relation chain. Do not add an unused value or declaration whose consumer path is absent from the supplied evidence. State a postcondition at the contract boundary that the change is intended to restore; do not treat merely adding a configuration key as sufficient when no consuming template or code is evidenced. Treat declared_artifacts as exact external input contracts. Copy configuration keys, annotation names, command-line flags, paths and literal values verbatim from their supplied content; do not rename a key or invent a semantically similar spelling. When a source field or parser is introduced for a declared input, its spelling must match the declared artifact exactly, and the plan must preserve that binding through each production consumer. Preserve downstream type contracts when carrying a scalar setting. For a timeout or duration whose zero value is the existing unset/default behavior, follow the consumer's established value type (normally time.Duration) through every carrier; do not invent pointer optionality merely to represent absence unless the supplied source or declared contract explicitly requires nil. When the requirement names a protocol verb or request branch, the selected target locator must include the exact owning branch and literal invocation in current source, not an adjacent send path that happens to share the file. If the supplied source excerpts do not contain the named protocol literal or owning symbol, do not substitute a neighbouring function with a similar file or role. Return NEEDS_EVIDENCE with a locatable search_term for the exact literal/symbol so the bounded retrieval extension can deliver the missing branch before creating an executable change. For a configuration value that crosses a public Config into an internal runtime carrier and then a processor or binding constructor, plan every evidenced bridge edge, including the internal conversion and runtime construction site. Do not assume a field added to Config reaches an internalConfig or processor automatically; if the runtime constructor is outside the supplied span, request its exact source evidence before finalizing the plan. When a nullable or pointer-valued field represents observed state, distinguish an absent declaration from a requested declaration whose external state is absent: preserve nil only when the supplied requirement and source contract make nil mean unset or not requested, and use the source-supported explicit false, empty, or other sentinel when the requirement says those states must remain distinguishable. Do not collapse these states merely because both provider responses are empty. Every planned postcondition must cite the atomic obligation IDs it restores, as well as its relation_refs. Preserve or leave open each atom not repaired this round by citing that atom in the matching preserve_constraints or open_obligations entry. Do not treat a test-only edit as restoration of a production relation; tests may be supplementary changes but cannot replace the production change or its postcondition. outcome_coverage.preserve_required contains outcome IDs whose already satisfied parts must have explicit preserve_constraints entries. open_obligations do not substitute for those preservation constraints. For an outcome containing both failed and passing predicates, preserve the supported passing predicates, plan the failed ones, and retain genuinely unverified residuals as open; do not delete a preservation requirement to satisfy validation. If no changes are planned, preservation_impact must use GLOBAL with empty change_refs rather than referring to absent changes. If planning needs additional evidence, return NEEDS_EVIDENCE with no executable changes and explicit open obligations. When you can locate the missing evidence, include evidence_gaps with id, summary and locator_hint.path, locator_hint.symbol or locator_hint.search_term. This shares the single Diagnosis extension allowance; it does not create a new round or replenish budgets. Otherwise omit evidence_gaps or return an empty array. Make every action specific enough for a separate executor: identify the production consumer and intended binding/state change in semantic_action, and preserve the requirement trigger/scope in intent. Use depends_on only for real prerequisites. Do not restate 'fix configuration' as the entire action or embed full implementation code. When reordering a production block, identify where every referenced input is initialized and remains in scope. Place the block only after those evidenced prerequisites and before the dependent behavior; a source line naming one prerequisite does not prove all inputs are available. Preserve error handling and guards when describing the move. Each P must state the actual observable boundary in planned_check/check_scope. Set verification_kind to PUBLIC_STRUCTURE, PUBLIC_BEHAVIOR, BUILD_ONLY, NOT_PUBLICLY_OBSERVABLE or UNKNOWN according to the declared public capabilities. A behavior P is not BUILD_ONLY merely because only builds are available. Unobservable behavior remains open to verification but does not prevent an otherwise supported executable change. Do not invent a new probe, command or hidden fixture. Preserve all supported atoms not repaired by this change. Review each atom against its original wording and trigger/object/preservation scope before planning. For each already evidenced production branch relevant to the same obligation, state in semantic_action/intent whether it is changed, remains valid with supporting rationale, or remains unresolved; do not equate an exact target with complete branch coverage. A broad owning-function obligation cannot silently narrow to one validator or one execution mode. No whole-repository branch enumeration is required. For declared-input equality use verification_kind=DECLARED_INPUT_EQUALITY and comparison_requirements binding every required artifact_id/input_pointer/output_pointer before execution. Use one P per scenario/resource when needed. Bindings contain paths, never expected values; incomplete or unavailable bindings remain UNKNOWN. Use verification_scope with scenario/resource identities when supplied by public artifacts; do not guess missing identities. Apply the appropriate verification kind to preservation and open obligations too. Before proposing reuse or transfer of runtime objects, inspect their ownership, cancellation, timer/channel lifetime, route/input binding and synchronization contracts in the supplied source. Transferring a map of pointers does not establish that the pointed-to objects remain usable under the replacement owner. If this repair strategy depends on a missing lifecycle contract, use the existing NEEDS_EVIDENCE extension with exact symbols rather than treating a proposed helper API as evidence that the strategy is safe. Preserve all source-supported behavior and retain unverified parts explicitly. When a change narrows a collection passed to a consumer, trace the complete collection through every relevant output/writeback branch. State how items excluded from that consumer remain available where preservation requires them. Preserving an existing assignment or helper sequence is not sufficient when its inputs or activation conditions change. Align initialization, helper use and cleanup with the same applicable conditions, or explain a supported alternative. Preserve required behavior rather than freezing a source statement that conflicts with the new selection. Use JSON Pointer strings: empty string for the root, otherwise begin with / (for example /settings/value or /items/0/value). Escape ~ as ~0 and / as ~1 inside a key. Dot paths, filenames and URI fragments are not JSON Pointers. A literal dot or # in a key is allowed after the leading /. Do not guess missing fields or change predeclared bindings during review. declared_artifacts are immutable read-only public inputs. Use supplied content verbatim for configuration keys, annotation names, flags, paths and literal values. Input delivery does not prove that production consumes the input, grant edit permission or add evidence IDs; production bindings still require the supplied source evidence.
